availability.note: CarsGuide 4 Sep 2026 launch review lists both grades, Pro 4X4 and X 4X4, as MSRP-priced current models; carsales research page shows indicative drive-away ranges by state for both grades (release April 2026, showrooms from Aug 2026 per GoAuto). JAC's own site (jacmotors.com.au) returned a 503 / JS redirect to /lander throughout, so no manufacturer configurator was readable. No evidence of a Victoria-specific restriction found. Cab-chassis (Pro/Oasis-based, unpriced) excluded.

listPrice.note: CarsGuide: 'Pro 4X4 $49,988' MSRP excluding on-road costs; CarExpert news 10 Jul 2026 '$49,988 before on-road costs'; GoAuto '$49,988 + ORC'. JAC's own price list unreachable (site down). Cross-check: carsales indicative drive-away Pro $51,537-$55,274 brackets the app's VIC ute drive-away of $52,296 for this list. Rejected CarExpert showroom 'Driveaway $47,676' (Sydney): identical for both grades and below the list price, a data error. No current price campaign found (launch offer is a charger/$500 voucher only, to 31 Dec 2026).

batteryKwh.note: CarExpert spec grid labels 31.2 kWh 'usable'; every other source (CarsGuide, 4X4 Australia, EV Central, carsales) quotes 31.2kWh LFP unlabelled; GoAuto once said 32kWh. Usable vs gross not settled by a manufacturer source.

rangeKm.note: EV Central '100km NEDC'; CarExpert 2026 news 'up to 100km based on NEDC testing'. No WLTP figure found: the T9 PHEV is not sold in a WLTP market (Malaysia/AU/China). Measured: CarsGuide ~80km, EV Central 75-80km.

consumptionKwhPer100km.note: batteryKwh / rangeKm x 100 = 31.2 / 100 x 100; no published EV-mode figure (EV Central spec sheet 'TBA'). Tautological against the cross-check.

combinedRangeKm.note: rangeKm + tank / fuelConsumptionL100km x 100 = 100 + 77 / 8.5 x 100 = 1006. Tank 77L per CarExpert spec page, 4X4 Australia, EV Central, carsales. JAC's own claim is 1005km NEDC (4X4 Australia).

fuelConsumptionL100km.note: No published charge-sustaining figure. Derived from JAC's claimed 1005km NEDC total range with 100km EV range and 77L tank: (1005-100)/77 = 11.75 km/L = 8.51 L/100km. Same method as the sibling gwm-cannon-phev (8.1). Real-world evidence is worse: EV Central ~14 L/100km with the engine driving, CarsGuide ~9.5 mixed (partly EV), 4X4 Australia 6.2 on test (with charging), EV Central pre-production estimate ~10.

isFuelEfficientForLct.note: JAC combined label 1.6 L/100km (NEDC), at or below 3.5.

isGreenForVicDuty.note: Ute: field rules require false on every ute row; Victoria charges utes as goods vehicles (isNonPassengerForVicDuty true).

bootLitresSeatsUp.note: Tub litres unpublished. CarExpert spec page: load length 1520mm, width 1590mm, height 470mm (same in carsales research). 1520 x 1590 x 470 = 1136 L; reads 10-20% high because arches are ignored. Siblings: Cannon PHEV 1196, Shark 6 1200, Ranger PHEV 1160.

towKg.note: 'Braked 3,500 kg, unbraked 750 kg'; CarsGuide and EV Central '3,500kg braked'; CarExpert FAQ says shared by all variants. JAC technical sheet unreachable (site down). GCM 6430kg per 4X4 Australia.

warrantyYears.note: Vehicle 7 years, no km limit; battery 8 years/150,000km. CarExpert review: 7yr/unlimited for all buyer types including commercial; capped servicing and roadside need JAC servicing but the warranty term does not.

insuranceAnnual.note: Anchored to gwm-cannon-phev-lux (1700 at $48,716) and ford-ranger-phev-xl (1700 at $56,515); +50 for a low-volume new brand with uncertain parts supply and 360kW claimed output.

depreciationCurve.note: New brand to the dataset; one curve for all JAC rows. Chose the low-volume curve held by KGM (kgm-musso-ev) rather than the GWM/Chery new-Chinese curve [1,0.7,...]: JAC is a small distributor-run brand with a thin network, its diesel T9 was cut by $3,500 cashback in its first year-end run-out (CarExpert, Nov 2025), the Hunter is a first-year nameplate with no resale history. Steeper than GWM, which has an established ute resale market (Cannon diesel).
